École Sainte-Cécile and École La Petite-Patrie are francophone public elementary schools of the
Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM), on either side of the boundary between
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. They sit 537 m apart, so a
family house-hunting between Jean-Talon and Beaubien is plausibly in reach of both. This report
takes them together and describes them in three layers: the schools themselves, the kilometre
around each, and what a three-bedroom home there costs to buy or rent this month.

Because the two circles overlap heavily, the interesting differences are small and local: which
park falls inside, how far the métro is, and which side of the borough line a tax bill lands on.
Two nearby schools are carried through the tables as comparators — **École La Mennais**, 444 m
from La Petite-Patrie on Saint-Denis, and **École Louis-Hippolyte-Lafontaine**, about 2.5 km
south on rue Berri in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, included as a contrast rather than as a neighbour.

::: {.callout-important}
## Not a ranking

Each zone metric is shown with its decile among the 229 francophone public elementary schools on
the island outside the West Island, marked [d1]{.decile-low} to [d3]{.decile-low} for the lowest
three tenths, [d4]{.decile-mid} to [d7]{.decile-mid} for the middle, and [d8]{.decile-high} to
[d10]{.decile-high} for the top three. A high decile means a high value, nothing
more, so the label says which way is favourable for a family: ▲ higher is favourable (children,
parks, stations), ▼ lower is favourable (crime, collisions, deprivation, cost), and rows with no
glyph are descriptive. On the ▲ and ▼ rows the most favourable of the compared zones is [shaded]{.best}.
The report computes no composite score, and the IMSE is a socioeconomic index of the pupils enrolled,
not a measure of academic performance.
:::

# The schools

Neither school is on the CSSDM's list of programmes et volets particuliers, and neither site
describes a selective stream: both are ordinary neighbourhood schools that take pupils by
address, with the CSSDM's *libre choix* applying if places remain after territory residents and
siblings.[^sc-adm][^lpp-adm] That makes them a different proposition from the IB, arts and
alternative schools catalogued elsewhere in this project — there is no application gate to plan
for, only an address.

Both school websites return HTTP 403 to anything that is not a browser, as several
`cssdm.gouv.qc.ca` school sites do. Facts drawn from their indexed pages rather than from a page
that loaded are marked *unverified* below.

: École Sainte-Cécile; facts marked *unverified* could not be confirmed on a page that loaded {#tbl-school-sc}

The schoolyard was rebuilt for $5M and inaugurated on 27 September 2022: a running track, soccer
and basketball surfaces, an outdoor classroom, rainwater management and soil rehabilitation, with
44 trees and 73 shrubs planted against the heat island.[^yard] The school also has a small
municipal park carrying its name immediately adjacent, which is why @tbl-parks treats its
kilometre generously.

::: {.callout-important}
## The second address is a transition school, not a relocation

École La Petite-Patrie was created in 2006 by merging two neighbourhood schools, the pavillons
Notre-Dame-de-la-Défense and Saint-Jean-de-la-Croix.[^lpp-ecole] In 2012 the
Saint-Jean-de-la-Croix building at 35 rue Saint-Zotique Est was converted into a CSSDM
*école de transition*, a building kept available to house schools whose own premises are being
repaired; about 150 pupils were moved at the time, the second-cycle classes into the
Notre-Dame-de-la-Défense pavilion.[^metro2012] It is still in that role today: the CSSDM's
register of relocated schools lists **École Félix-Leclerc**, whose home is 6055 avenue Darlington
in Côte-des-Neiges, as partially relocated to 35 rue Saint-Zotique Est.[^deloc]

So La Petite-Patrie is the host, not a relocated school. Its own pupils are at 6841 avenue
Henri-Julien, and that address anchors its zone throughout this report. No temporary-site column
is needed.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Why École Félix-Leclerc is not used as a comparator

Félix-Leclerc [762134] looks like the closest school to La Petite-Patrie — 345 m — but only
because the MEQ file currently gives its principal point as the transition building on rue
Saint-Zotique. Its home building is 6055 avenue Darlington, 2.9 km southwest in Côte-des-Neiges.
Profiling the kilometre around its MEQ point would describe the neighbourhood its pupils commute
to during works, not the one a family would move to. It is left out for that reason.
:::

## What the indices say

The MEQ's IMSE places Sainte-Cécile in decile 3 and La Petite-Patrie in decile 4 for 2025-2026
(1 = most advantaged, 10 = most disadvantaged; 8 to 10 is the official *milieu défavorisé*). It
is built from the enrolled pupils' parents' education and employment, not from test results, and
Quebec publishes no academic ranking of elementary schools. Both schools sit in decile 8 on the
SFR, the low-income-threshold index, which is the more volatile of the two.

The two indices disagree in the usual direction here: the IMSE deciles are mid-to-low while the
SFR deciles are high, and the census figures for the residents of the kilometre (@tbl-people)
show median household income slightly above the island median. An index of the families who
actually enrol is not an index of the households who live nearby, and in central boroughs with
many renters, small households and private-school options the two routinely part company.

# The zone

Each zone is a circle of one kilometre around the school building, a stand-in for the catchment
polygon that exists only in the service centre's finder and PDF maps. At 537 m apart, the
Sainte-Cécile and La Petite-Patrie circles share most of their area; La Mennais, 444 m east of La
Petite-Patrie, overlaps both. Louis-Hippolyte-Lafontaine is the one genuinely separate zone in
the tables.

: Who lives within 1 km of the school (2021 census, aggregated over dissemination areas whose centroid falls in the circle) {#tbl-people}
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the table

All four zones are dense and short of children: the 0-to-14 share and the share of households
with children sit in the bottom two deciles everywhere, against an island median near a third of
households. That is the central-Montreal pattern rather than anything about these schools, and it
is the line a family moving from a suburb will notice first. Household income is at or a little
above the island median in the two subject zones and drifts down towards the Plateau comparator,
where the low-income share is markedly higher. French spoken most often at home is well above the
island median in all four, highest around La Petite-Patrie and La Mennais. Residential turnover
is high everywhere — more than half of residents moved within five years — which is what a rental
stock of this size produces.
:::

## Social deprivation is high across central Montreal

The INSPQ social axis counts people living alone and lone-parent families, which the dense
central boroughs are full of; read it with the households-with-children line of @tbl-people.
All four zones sit far above the island median on the social axis and far below it on the
material axis, and the city's own equity index separates them barely at all.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the table

All four zones report more incidents per resident than the island median, which is normal for
zones containing commercial strips and métro stations — Jean-Talon, De Castelnau and Parc for
Sainte-Cécile, Beaubien for La Mennais. The two subject zones are close to each other on every
line; the Plateau comparator is higher on the total and much higher on theft from vehicles. The
violent-crime line is in the top decile for the two subjects and their close neighbour, at a
rate roughly double the island median, and it is worth reading against the low absolute counts
such rates come from. The pedestrian and cyclist line is the one a parent walking a child to
school should weigh: all four are in the top decile, and Sainte-Cécile's 500 m circle takes in
the Jean-Talon and Saint-Laurent arterials.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## What these two datasets cannot say

The city states the incident file is not official SPVM statistics; positions are moved to the
nearest intersection and 17% of incidents have no coordinates and are absent from the rates.
The collision extract ends in 2021; its last two years are pandemic years. Both are rates of
reported events, not of risk.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the tables

The stock is the classic Petite-Patrie–Villeray mix: plex units are the largest single category
in the three northern zones, single-family houses are near-absent, and the median building dates
from between the wars. Assessed values and 2026 tax bills sit in the ninth decile across all four
zones for every property type, roughly 40% above the island median for a single-family house and
20% above it for a plex. The two subject zones are marginally cheaper than the Plateau comparator
on every line, though the gap is small relative to the spread within any one zone. The effective
tax rate is flat at about two-thirds of a percent across the island, so the bill differences track
the assessments rather than any borough's rate. Assessed values reflect the July 2024 market and
lag transactions by roughly eighteen months.
:::

| ▲ Métro and REM stations inside the zone | stations | [3 [d9]{.decile-high}]{.best} | [3 [d9]{.decile-high}]{.best} | [3 [d9]{.decile-high}]{.best} | [3 [d9]{.decile-high}]{.best} | 0 |
| ▲ Park area | % of zone | 9.2 [d7]{.decile-mid} | 2.8 [d1]{.decile-low} | 4.7 [d3]{.decile-low} | [12.9 [d9]{.decile-high}]{.best} | 6.6 |
| ▲ Park area per 1 000 residents | ha | 0.80 [d4]{.decile-mid} | 0.25 [d1]{.decile-low} | 0.46 [d2]{.decile-low} | [0.96 [d5]{.decile-mid}]{.best} | 0.96 |

: Parks and rapid transit within 1 km: large parks and borough parks (Ville de Montréal), métro and REM stations (OpenStreetMap contributors) {#tbl-parks}
:::

Parks are where the two subject zones part company most clearly. Sainte-Cécile's circle takes in
**parc Jarry** — 35 ha, 369 m from the school door — plus the small **parc Sainte-Cécile**
immediately beside the building, which is why its park share sits above the island median. La
Petite-Patrie's circle reaches parc Jarry only at its far northern edge, 883 m away, so its own
kilometre is served by the **Réseau Vert** linear park (693 m) and parc Sainte-Cécile (438 m), and
lands in the bottom decile on both park measures. La Mennais draws on **parc Père-Marquette**
(838 m); Louis-Hippolyte-Lafontaine has **parc La Fontaine** 391 m away, which is what puts it in
the ninth decile.

Rapid transit is strong for all four: each kilometre contains three métro stations, against an
island median of none. La Mennais is 65 m from Beaubien on the orange line, Sainte-Cécile 248 m
from Jean-Talon, Louis-Hippolyte-Lafontaine 322 m from Mont-Royal, and La Petite-Patrie 450 m
from Beaubien — every one of them in the bottom decile for distance, meaning closer than almost
any school on the island.

## Listings expire — and this snapshot is thinner than usual

These are 3+ bedroom listings found on 2026-09-26 within about a kilometre of the two schools,
chosen for variety of type rather than as a sample; prices are asking prices, and the section is
not refreshed when the post is republished. This run was unusually constrained: Centris,
DuProprio and Realtor.ca all refuse individual listing pages to anything that is not a browser,
so every figure here comes from a search-result snippet and is marked *unverified*, and bedroom
counts are missing for the plex listings, where the relevant number is the bedrooms in the
owner-occupied unit rather than in the building. Treat the table as four and four examples of
what was on the market, nothing more. For a durable benchmark use the assessed values in
@tbl-cost.
:::

# Sources and caveats

- **School facts**: the CSSDM pages linked in the footnotes, opened 2026-09-26. Both school
  websites return HTTP 403 to non-browser clients, so program, projet éducatif, admission
  wording and the AMPLI point of service are *unverified*, taken from search-index extracts. The
  schoolyard communiqué, the register of relocated schools and the 2012 *Journal Métro* article
  did load and are verified.
- **IMSE/SFR**: MEQ, *Indices de défavorisation*, Données Québec, school year 2025-2026.
- **Zone tables**: `scripts/zone_stats.py` on open data fetched 2026-09-18 (Ville de Montréal,
  Données Québec, INSPQ, Statistics Canada 2021 Census); 65 dissemination areas for
  Sainte-Cécile, 61 for La Petite-Patrie, 60 for La Mennais and 75 for
  Louis-Hippolyte-Lafontaine, assigned by centroid; the IEMV covers 100% of residents in all four
  zones and tax bills matched for 99.8% to 99.9% of units. Census 2021 is five years old;
  assessed values reflect the July 2024 market.
- **Parks named above**: Ville de Montréal *espaces verts*, distances measured from the school
  point in the same run.
- **Listings**: as seen on Centris.ca on 2026-09-26, from search-result snippets only.
- **Deciles**: among 229 in-scope schools, from `data/derived/zone_stats_all.parquet`.

# Conclusion

Four readings, in the order a parent weighs them. Each states what the tables show, not a verdict.

**School.** Two CSSDM neighbourhood schools with no selective stream and no application gate:
admission is by address, with *libre choix* only if places remain (@tbl-school-sc,
@tbl-school-lpp). Sainte-Cécile is the larger of the two and has a rebuilt schoolyard from 2022;
La Petite-Patrie is smaller, hosts the CSSDM's réseau Centre AMPLI classes, and holds a second
MEQ address that is a transition building for another school rather than a sign of works on its
own. IMSE deciles are 3 and 4, SFR decile 8 for both — a socioeconomic index of enrolled pupils,
not a measure of academic performance.

**Safety.** Both kilometres report crime above the island median on every category, with violent
crime in the top decile and pedestrian and cyclist victims in the top decile within 500 m
(@tbl-safety). The two subject zones are close to each other and below the Plateau comparator on
the total. Both datasets are counts of reported events with known coverage gaps.

**Livability.** Dense, heavily rented, strongly French-speaking, and short of children by island
standards, with high turnover (@tbl-people, @tbl-indices). Transit is the standout: three métro
stations in every kilometre and walking distance to the orange line from all four schools. Parks
are where the two subjects diverge — parc Jarry sits inside Sainte-Cécile's circle and only
clips La Petite-Patrie's (@tbl-parks).

**Affordability.** Plex-dominated prewar stock with almost no single-family houses; assessed
values and 2026 tax bills in the ninth decile for every property type, above the island median
by a wide margin (@tbl-stock, @tbl-cost). The month's listings are consistent with that but too
few and too lightly verified to add much (@tbl-for-sale, @tbl-for-rent).

Next steps for these schools:

1. **Confirm the catchment** on the CSSDM finder for candidate addresses. The boundary between
   the two schools runs somewhere inside this overlap and the circle is only a stand-in; an
   address 537 m from both is not necessarily eligible for either one you prefer.
2. **Watch the January registration window** — registration runs through January at the school
   secretariat for the following school year.
3. **Check whether 35 rue Saint-Zotique Est is still a transition building** before reading
   anything into La Petite-Patrie's second MEQ address; Félix-Leclerc's occupancy ends when its
   Darlington works do.
4. **What this report does not yet cover**: childcare places, transit frequency, heat islands,
   rents by CMHC zone, and the secondary school the zone feeds.

::: {.callout-important}
## Bottom line

These two schools are close enough that the choice between them is mostly a choice of street
rather than of neighbourhood: the census, safety and cost tables barely separate them, and the
clearest difference is that parc Jarry falls inside one kilometre and not the other. The thing to
verify before acting is the catchment boundary on the CSSDM finder — neither school takes pupils
on preference alone, and in this overlap an address decides which of the two is yours.
:::
